# Survey Questionnaire — English Version

This document provides the English representation of the questionnaire used in the study.

**Note:** SQ01 is automatically generated timestamp metadata. SQ02–SQ30 are questionnaire content. Structured categories listed below correspond to categories observed in the analytical export. Post-hoc analytical mappings are documented separately in `traceability/category_mapping.csv`.

## Questionnaire

1. **SQ01 — Timestamp**  
   Automatically generated metadata.

2. **SQ02 — Participant profile (education level)**  
   Single choice. Observed categories: Technical education; Bachelor's degree; Specialization; Master's degree; PhD; Postdoctoral.

3. **SQ03 — How many years of experience do you have in embedded systems?**  
   Single choice. Observed categories: Less than 1 year; 1–3 years; 3–5 years; 5–10 years; More than 10 years.

4. **SQ04 — What is your current role in the company?**  
   Categorical response.

5. **SQ05 — Which industry domain does your company operate in?**  
   Categorical response.

6. **SQ06 — In which country do you work?**  
   Categorical/free-text response.

7. **SQ07 — Which characteristics do you consider most important in embedded software maintenance?**  
   Multiple choice. Observed categories: Stability; Efficiency; Flexibility; Ease of Integration; Security; Code Readability.

8. **SQ08 — Which strategies do you use for embedded software maintenance?**  
   Multiple choice with free-text additions. Observed structured categories: Code Refactoring; Code Review; Obsolescence Analysis; Configuration Management; Automated Testing.

9. **SQ09 — What are the main difficulties encountered in embedded software maintenance?**  
   Multiple choice. Observed categories: Integration of New Technologies; Design Complexity; Hardware Limitations; Lack of Documentation; Frequent Rework.

10. **SQ10 — Have you ever used a unified model integrating multiple maintenance and evolution strategies?**  
    Single choice: Yes; No.

11. **SQ11 — Which components do you consider essential for a unified maintenance and evolution model?**  
    Multiple choice. Observed categories: Code Inspection; Code Refactoring; Obsolescence Analysis; Configuration Management; Automated Testing; Technical Debt Review.

12. **SQ12 — In your experience, what are the benefits of a unified model for software maintenance and evolution?**  
    Multiple choice with free-text addition. Observed structured categories: Greater Efficiency; Improved Process Coordination; Cost Reduction; Improved Software Quality; Defect Reduction.

13. **SQ13 — Which software tools do you use for embedded software maintenance?**  
    Multiple-value response.

14. **SQ14 — How do you evaluate the effectiveness of these tools in supporting embedded-software maintenance and evolution?**  
    Ordinal single choice. Observed categories: Slightly Effective; Neutral; Effective; Very Effective.

15. **SQ15 — Have you compared different software tools for maintenance?**  
    Single choice: Yes; No.

16. **SQ16 — If yes, which tool was the most effective?**  
    Open conditional follow-up.

17. **SQ17 — What are the main difficulties you face when applying maintenance strategies?**  
    Multiple choice with free-text additions. Observed structured categories: Lack of Adequate Tools; Code Complexity; Time Constraints; Lack of Training; Budget Constraints.

18. **SQ18 — Which methods do you use to overcome these difficulties?**  
    Multiple choice with free-text additions. Observed structured categories: Additional Training; Specialized Tools; Collaboration with Specialists; Process Automation; Documentation Improvement.

19. **SQ19 — Do you believe that integrating new technologies facilitates or hinders software maintenance?**  
    Single choice. Observed categories: Facilitates; Hinders; Depends on the Technology; Not Sure.

20. **SQ20 — Which embedded-software lifecycle phases can be affected by maintenance?**  
    Multiple choice. Observed categories: Planning; Requirements; Design; Implementation; Testing; Discontinuation.

21. **SQ21 — How are these lifecycle phases affected?**  
    Open response.

22. **SQ22 — What are the main challenges during embedded-software maintenance planning?**  
    Multiple choice with free-text additions. Observed structured categories: Forecasting Future Issues; Resource Allocation; Requirements Identification; Team Coordination; Integration of New Technologies.

23. **SQ23 — Have you ever had to perform rework due to inadequate planning in the initial phase?**  
    Single choice: Yes; No.

24. **SQ24 — Frequency with which rework occurred**  
    Open conditional follow-up.

25. **SQ25 — Which metrics do you consider important for evaluating embedded-software maintenance?**  
    Multiple choice with free-text additions. Observed structured categories: Code Quality; Maintenance Time; Defect Reduction; Tool Effectiveness; Real-Time Performance; Energy Consumption.

26. **SQ26 — How do you measure real-time performance and energy consumption in the maintenance context?**  
    Multiple choice with free-text additions. Observed structured categories: Monitoring Tools; Specific Tests; Manual Evaluation; Benchmarking.

27. **SQ27 — What difficulties do you face in standardizing metrics for embedded-software maintenance?**  
    Multiple choice with free-text additions. Observed structured categories: System Variety; Lack of Tools; Metric Complexity; Team Resistance.

28. **SQ28 — Do you use agile methodologies (e.g., Scrum or XP) in your embedded-software projects?**  
    Single choice: Yes; No.

29. **SQ29 — Which adaptations are necessary to apply agile methodologies to embedded systems?**  
    Multiple choice with free-text additions. Observed structured categories: Sprint Customization; Continuous Integration; Documentation Adjustments; Role Redefinition.

30. **SQ30 — In your opinion, what are the benefits of agile methodologies in the embedded-software context?**  
    Multiple choice with free-text additions. Observed structured categories: Greater Flexibility; Better Response to Change; Increased Collaboration; Reduced Rework.
